lead.title: Therakos wins MDR certification for its CELLEX photopheresis system against immune-related adverse events from checkpoint inhibitors
lead.deck: The THERAKOS CELLEX system is now certified in Europe for adults with an inadequate response to corticosteroids facing immune-related adverse events (irAEs) from checkpoint-inhibitor immunotherapy, an indication the company presents as the first approved anywhere in the world. The clinical evidence remains modest (small series, the PRIA study, the ongoing PHOENIX-ECP trial): this is a market-access milestone rather than definitive proof.

milestone.title: FDA approves PerQseal Elite, the sutureless large-bore arterial closure device from Irish start-up Vivasure
milestone.summary: A fully bioabsorbable patch placed from inside the vessel, for structural heart and endovascular procedures using 14 to 22 F sheaths (openings up to 26 F). ELITE arterial study: 0% major complications (VARC-3) and mean hemostasis in under one minute.
milestone.why: Haemonetics acquired Vivasure in January 2026 and then secured the US PMA, with the CE mark dating from 2025: a textbook case of a European start-up being valued by a large group even before the FDA step.

deal.thesis: A pocket-size Micro Lab, spun out of the University of Glasgow, that measures several hormones in saliva within minutes. The round was led by Conduit EIS Impact Fund and Wrightwood (with Leo Capital, Embryo Ventures, Hermesa and Zinc VC) and funds equivalence studies, new markers and the regulatory file ahead of early-access devices in 2027.

brefsEurope.title: Siloton wins £8.4M from Innovate UK for its handheld GiraffeOCT imager
brefsEurope.summary: A two-year contract (Quantum Missions Primer programme) to design in-clinic and at-home versions and run the trials, including at Sunderland Specialist Eye Hospital. The company expects to save up to two years of development.

brefsEurope.title: 4Tissue raises €7M Series A and appoints Stéphanie Dupont as CEO
brefsEurope.summary: The Belgian medtech, which is developing a bioresorbable hydrogel for breast reconstruction, is funding its first-in-human study and the scale-up of its manufacturing.

word.definition: A cardiac ablation technique that destroys the cells behind an arrhythmia with brief high-voltage electrical pulses, rather than heat or cold.

parts.label: Catheter
parts.role: brings the electrodes into contact with heart tissue

parts.label: Mapping
parts.role: locates the areas to treat (pulmonary veins)

how.t: The catheter is guided into the atrium and locates the pulmonary veins, a frequent source of atrial fibrillation.
A pulsed electric field irreversibly opens the membranes of the targeted heart-muscle cells.
The treated tissue no longer conducts current: the arrhythmia is cut off from its triggers.

word.why: More selective for heart muscle than radiofrequency or cryoablation, PFA has become the racetrack of the majors (Boston Scientific, J&J, Abbott, Medtronic): the entry window for start-ups is narrowing, hence the appeal of differentiated catheters (integrated mapping, focal designs).
